title: Things to do in Nice: 5 places from old town to the sea
description: Plan a first visit to Nice with five places: the Promenade, old town, Castle Hill, Place Masséna and Port Lympia, plus a flexible walking route.
relatedQueries: places to visit in Nice France
intro: For a first visit to Nice, start with five places that connect different sides of the city: the Promenade des Anglais, the old town around Cours Saleya, Castle Hill, Place Masséna and Port Lympia. Together, they offer the open seafront, historic streets, a view from above, a central square and a working harbour. You do not need to tour the whole Riviera or arrange a museum visit to make this a satisfying introduction.

The useful decision is how much walking and climbing suits your group. Castle Hill changes the effort involved, while a break beside the sea or in the old town gives the route some breathing space. One flexible day can introduce the five places; two days allow more time to look around and eat without rushing. Confirm market arrangements, park opening and lift operation for your travel date, especially if you rely on a route without stairs.

sections.heading: 1. Promenade des Anglais: choose a stretch that suits your day
paragraphs: The Promenade des Anglais follows the Baie des Anges and provides one of the clearest ways to understand Nice’s position beside the sea. The tourist office describes a length of nearly seven kilometres. That figure is useful for planning: trying to walk the entire seafront before seeing the rest of the city can make a first day unnecessarily tiring. Choose a manageable stretch that works with your accommodation and your onward walk towards the old town.

Pause to observe the relationship between the walkway, beaches and buildings instead of treating the sea as a backdrop you pass at speed. Walking and resting here do not require a separate booked activity. Beach equipment, dining and other services have their own arrangements, however. The official history traces the promenade’s beginnings to an initiative supported by Lewis Way in 1824; it adds context to the name without requiring you to follow a formal heritage trail. Adjust your distance to the weather and the energy of the people travelling with you.

sections.heading: 2. Vieux Nice and Cours Saleya: spend time in the old town
paragraphs: Vieux Nice offers a different scale after the openness of the seafront. The official city guide highlights its streets and craft shops and includes Cours Saleya among the places associated with markets. Make this a small old-town walk with a clear reference point, rather than going in only to photograph a stall. The interest also lies in the surrounding facades, connecting streets and change of atmosphere as you step away from the water.

If seeing a particular market matters to you, check its calendar before choosing your arrival time. Different market activities do not necessarily operate under the same arrangements, and an archival photograph cannot establish what will be set up on your date. For food, compare menus and conditions before taking a table instead of pursuing an unverified must-visit restaurant. Keep entrances clear when stopping, and ask before taking close photographs of sellers or customers. A well-placed break here can make the next part of the itinerary more comfortable.

sections.heading: 3. Castle Hill: understand the city from above
paragraphs: The Colline du Château, usually called Castle Hill in English, is recommended here as a park and viewpoint rather than a furnished castle to tour. The tourist office describes the former citadel site becoming a public promenade and highlights its paths, trees, waterfall and views towards the bay, old town and harbour. The attraction is partly geographical: from above, you can connect the areas you have visited and decide which direction to explore next. Visibility remains dependent on the weather.

Plan the ascent before committing to it. The official Nice guide describes routes using stairs and streets, as well as a lift near Rue des Ponchettes. A lift’s existence does not guarantee that it is running at every moment or that every park path avoids slopes. If you need step-free access or are travelling with a pushchair, confirm the specific entrance and route. Check the park’s seasonal closing time and leave room to descend. The photograph shows a view from the hill, not a survey of all paths or a guarantee of present access conditions.

sections.heading: 4. Place Masséna: a square that helps join the city together
paragraphs: Place Masséna is a useful link between the seafront side of Nice and other parts of the centre. The tourist office’s route connects it with the old town and Promenade du Paillon, drawing attention to its facades. Spend a little time looking at the urban setting: the open space, buildings and connections between districts. The stop does not need a booked activity to contribute to your understanding of the city.

It is also a sensible place to reconsider your plan. If the hill has taken more energy than expected, pause before deciding whether to continue to the harbour. If your group would rather walk less, split the route over two days instead of treating every section as compulsory. Pay attention to signs and circulation areas when crossing the square; a broad open space does not mean that every part is suitable for standing still to take photographs. The image illustrates the facades and patterned paving, without suggesting the square is always clear of events or temporary installations.

sections.heading: 5. Port Lympia: another way to experience the waterfront
paragraphs: Port Lympia gives the visit a different finish from the beaches. The official route describes walks along several quays and mentions the traditional pointus boats associated with the harbour. There is no need to add a boat excursion simply because you have reached the port. Public waterfront paths already provide a chance to observe the relationship between the basins, boats, buildings and maritime activity. Give the overall setting as much attention as any particular vessel.

Choose how far to continue according to the time and energy you have left, and respect working areas or restricted access. An attractive harbour is still a place where people work and traffic moves. Do not go through closed gates to approach a boat or assume that a seasonal water crossing operates on your date. If you want a maritime service, check its operator, terms and weather arrangements independently. The archival photograph documents the harbour in 2011; it is not a promise that a named vessel will still be moored in the same place.

sections.heading: Arrange the walk around effort, access and your arrival point
paragraphs: Think in areas rather than following the article numbers as a compulsory sequence. You might begin on the eastern part of the Promenade, explore Cours Saleya, go up the hill if the access suits you, and descend towards the harbour. Leave Masséna for the return or another outing. Your accommodation, the light and park conditions can justify a different order; walking times will not be identical for every visitor.

If arriving or leaving by rail, check the exact station name on your ticket. The tourist office places Nice-Saint-Augustin in the Arenas district near the airport. Seeing Nice in a station name is not enough to assume that you will step out beside the old town. Check the connection to your accommodation with the relevant transport operator. For the walk, bring water and appropriate footwear, and dress for the forecast. Being beside the sea does not remove the effort of slopes or exposure to the weather.

sections.heading: Keep optional services and extra activities separate
paragraphs: Distinguish the places you walk through from services you decide to buy. This selection focuses on promenades, a park and public urban areas; it does not imply that transport, meals, beach equipment or other activities nearby are included. Read the current park information and budget separately for food, transfers and optional bookings. That is more useful than relying on a generic daily figure that cannot reflect your choices.

Choose a meal stop that fits the route rather than crossing the city for an unchecked recommendation. If rain or tiredness changes the day, shorten the outdoor sections and save places for tomorrow. This guide does not promise a museum visit as an instant substitute: opening, availability and exhibitions would need their own checks. If travelling elsewhere in France, the Paris guide offers a contrasting city stay, not a nearby excursion or an automatic extension of this Nice walk.

itinerary: Begin with a manageable section of the Promenade des Anglais and enter the old town around Cours Saleya. If a particular market is important, adapt the first part of the day to its confirmed calendar.
After a break, ascend Castle Hill only after checking access and opening. Continue towards Port Lympia if you have enough energy and time to return comfortably.

Use Place Masséna on your way back into the centre or save it for another outing. Over two days, separate seafront and old-town time from the hill and harbour, adapting the combination to your accommodation and mobility.

faq.question: Can you visit these five places in Nice in one day?
faq.answer: They can be combined in an organized day, but you do not need to walk the whole Promenade or every harbour quay. Two days make breaks easier and allow more flexibility for hill access, markets and weather.

faq.question: Does Castle Hill include a castle you can tour?
faq.answer: The recommended visit is to the park and its views, on the site of the former citadel. It is not presented as a furnished castle tour. Check seasonal opening and access before making the ascent.

faq.question: Do you have to climb all the stairs to reach Castle Hill?
faq.answer: The official guide mentions a lift near Rue des Ponchettes as well as walking routes. Confirm operation and the specific route if you need to avoid steps; a lift does not establish accessibility on every path.

faq.question: What should you check before visiting the Cours Saleya market?
faq.answer: Check the type of market and its calendar for your travel date. Do not assume that all stalls operate every day or that an archival image represents current activity. The surrounding old town remains worth exploring even if your preferred market is not taking place.

conclusion: Nice makes a rewarding first visit when five different experiences connect: the Promenade’s horizon, the old town’s smaller scale, the hill’s perspective, Masséna’s urban setting and the harbour landscape. Adjust their order to your arrival point, confirm arrangements that depend on opening or operation, and allow room for breaks. This balance gives you more attention for the city and keeps a Riviera visit from becoming a hurried sequence of photographs.
